messages:
Aisha S.: Heads-up — after last night's RBAC rollout I'm seeing a big spike of SAST 'no owner' failures for infra libs and DAST jobs skipped due to KMS decrypt errors. Audit logs for the scanner SA look like they have a gap.

Aisha S.: ```CI-bot: sast-check (infra) FAILED
error: ownership lookup: no CODEOWNER for path infra/compute/*
dast-run: failed to unwrap secrets: permissions denied (KMS:Decrypt)
``` 

Ravi K.: cc @sec-oncall — what exactly changed in the RBAC PR? I thought we only removed a broad group binding.

Maria D.: I opened the RBAC PR to reduce blast radius — removed group:ci-broad-write from a couple projects. Did I accidentally remove scanner SA from any bindings? I checked quickly but can re-check.

sec-oncall: Can someone paste the scanner SA name and current IAM bindings? also exact timestamps for the failures.

Aisha S.: Scanner SA: scanner-service@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com. Failures around 2024-11-20T03:10:00Z - 03:40:00Z. I grabbed the policy and scanner-service is NOT listed as a kms decryptor — only deploy-bot group still has roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter.

Ravi K.: That would explain the DAST KMS decrypt errors. For the SAST ownership hits: our ownership lookup service needs repo read to evaluate CODEOWNERS + blame; if scanner lost repo read, it returns no owner.

Maria D.: I can revert the single group-remove on the binding that affected CI. Re-adding scanner-service to the KMS IAM binding now.

Maria D.: ```gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-inference \
  --member=serviceAccount:scanner-service@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
``` 

CI-bot: deploy-tooling: IAM binding applied.

Aisha S.: Kicked off re-runs. SASTs re-triggering; some infra jobs passed but ~20 PRs still show 'no owner'. Might be ownership service cache returning stale data.

Ravi K.: Try clearing the owner-service cache for the repo: /internal/owner-service/cache/clear redwood-monorepo

Maria D.: Cleared cache and triggered SAST re-checks.

CI-bot: sast-check re-run queued for infra/*

sec-oncall: About the audit log gap — check if the log sink/export was temporarily disabled or if rotation coincided with a retention purge. If the scanner used KMS-wrapped ephemeral keys, rotation may orphan older wrapped keys until grants are re-provisioned which also causes missing decrypt events.

Aisha S.: Good call. I see logs before 03:09 and after 03:41 but nothing between. I'll collect request ids and slices and attach to the incident ticket.

Ravi K.: For quick mitigation I propose pipeline fallbacks: if ownership lookup fails, fallback to in-repo CODEOWNERS file and label as 'owner-inferred' (do not block). Create an issue and we can tighten later.

Maria D.: I'll draft that fallback PR. Also drafting a short postmortem with timeline + the exact gcloud commands used to rehydrate access.

sec-oncall: Please escalate the missing audit logs to cloud support if we can't recover them internally — include the time window and request ids. Also add a pre-rotation checklist item: ensure scanner/service accounts maintain temporary decrypt/read grants until migration is verified.

Aisha S.: Adding product teams affected: @payments @billing — your PRs may be blocked; rebase once checks clear.

payments-lead: Thanks for the heads-up. We'll rebase and re-run tests — please ping when the majority of SASTs pass.

Aisha S.: Follow-ups I will open as tickets: 1) revert-or-stabilize-binding (short term) 2) add pre-rotation checklist to infra runbook 3) pipeline fallback PR for owner-service 4) postmortem + audit-scope ticket for cloud support. Assigning to oncall+infra owners.

Ravi K.: I'll draft the pipeline PR and reference these tickets.

Maria D.: Reverted RBAC change permanently for the scanner-service until we have the checklist. Posting the postmortem draft in #incidents shortly.

sec-oncall: :thumbsup: thanks all. Keep this thread updated with ticket links and support case numbers.
